$comment: Witnessed firing on the VS Code Copilot IDE agent (v1.129.1, commit 8a7abeba, x64) on 2026-07-20, with the version + hooks-wrapper + bash/cwd/timeoutSec shape below. The witnessed firing config carried NO extra keys — strip this "$comment" if your Copilot surface rejects unknown top-level keys. CLI and cloud Copilot surfaces are UNVERIFIED (their schema may differ; no claim transfers to them). Design intent: validate on sessionStart, commit on postToolUse, sessionEnd is a bonus; every command is idempotent and no-op-safe at any frequency. cwd '.' is the workspace root so plain relative git paths work. ACTIVATION: on a freshly-created workspace, postToolUse may not auto-fire immediately even after trusting the folder and reloading — see README's 'Hook activation caveat' section. ESTATE-KEY GUARD (#60): both commit-bearing hooks (postToolUse, sessionEnd) no-op unless 'git config --local harness.estate' is 'true' — the positive-identity key install.sh writes into the estate's own .git/config, which the worktree cannot reach or forge, so the hook can never auto-commit into a nested foreign project repo (e.g. under Github/). sessionStart is read-only and stays unguarded. WORK MAP: observe navigation in a separate second sessionStart command so a warning-only helper cannot mask the existing validator's failure. Missing Python or helper failures emit a NOTE and never gate work; --strict is deliberately absent. The separator has its own line, and each entry's 'powershell' variant its own continuation line, so every original 'bash' command stays byte-for-byte. WINDOWS (#339): Copilot runs an entry's 'powershell' command on Windows, where a bare `bash` resolves to System32's WSL launcher and fails whenever WSL is off. Each variant therefore finds Git Bash (beside git.exe, else under Program Files), writes THAT entry's own 'bash' text, read back from .github/hooks/harness.json, to a temp file (UTF-8 without a BOM: a pipe from Windows PowerShell can prepend one), runs it, passes its exit code on and deletes the file; so every command keeps one home, and without Git Bash the hook prints a NOTE and does nothing. Witnessed by hand from Windows PowerShell 5.1 on 2026-10-28: all four variants ran and both commit hooks committed. An --upgrade keeps an estate's existing harness.json: an estate installed before #339 copies this file over it once (it holds no per-estate values).

sessionStart.powershell: $g = Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $b = ''; if ($g) { $b = Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $g.Source)) 'bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not ($b -and (Test-Path $b))) { $b = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Git\bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not (Test-Path $b)) { Write-Output 'NOTE [hooks]: Git Bash not found; this hook did not run.'; exit 0 }; $t = [IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t, (Get-Content -Raw .github/hooks/harness.json | ConvertFrom-Json).hooks.sessionStart[0].bash); & $b $t; $rc = $LASTEXITCODE; Remove-Item $t -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit $rc

sessionStart.bash:
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf 'NOTE [work-map]: python3 unavailable; navigation checks skipped.
'; elif [ ! -f _harness/scripts/check-work-map.py ]; then printf 'NOTE [work-map]: helper unavailable; navigation checks skipped.
'; else python3 _harness/scripts/check-work-map.py || printf 'NOTE [work-map]: helper could not complete; navigation coverage unavailable.
'; fi
sessionStart.powershell: $g = Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $b = ''; if ($g) { $b = Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $g.Source)) 'bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not ($b -and (Test-Path $b))) { $b = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Git\bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not (Test-Path $b)) { Write-Output 'NOTE [hooks]: Git Bash not found; this hook did not run.'; exit 0 }; $t = [IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t, (Get-Content -Raw .github/hooks/harness.json | ConvertFrom-Json).hooks.sessionStart[1].bash); & $b $t; $rc = $LASTEXITCODE; Remove-Item $t -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit $rc

postToolUse.bash: [ "$(git config --local harness.estate 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ] || exit 0; git add -A && git diff-index --quiet HEAD || git commit -q -m "auto-write $(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S): $(git diff --cached --name-only | tr '\n' ' ')"
postToolUse.powershell: $g = Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $b = ''; if ($g) { $b = Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $g.Source)) 'bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not ($b -and (Test-Path $b))) { $b = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Git\bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not (Test-Path $b)) { Write-Output 'NOTE [hooks]: Git Bash not found; this hook did not run.'; exit 0 }; $t = [IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t, (Get-Content -Raw .github/hooks/harness.json | ConvertFrom-Json).hooks.postToolUse[0].bash); & $b $t; $rc = $LASTEXITCODE; Remove-Item $t -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit $rc

sessionEnd.bash: [ "$(git config --local harness.estate 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ] || exit 0; bash _harness/scripts/check-ticket-log.sh; git add -A && git diff-index --quiet HEAD || git commit -q -m "auto-session-end $(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S): $(git diff --cached --name-only | tr '\n' ' ')"
sessionEnd.powershell: $g = Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $b = ''; if ($g) { $b = Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $g.Source)) 'bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not ($b -and (Test-Path $b))) { $b = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Git\bin\bash.exe' }; if (-not (Test-Path $b)) { Write-Output 'NOTE [hooks]: Git Bash not found; this hook did not run.'; exit 0 }; $t = [IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t, (Get-Content -Raw .github/hooks/harness.json | ConvertFrom-Json).hooks.sessionEnd[0].bash); & $b $t; $rc = $LASTEXITCODE; Remove-Item $t -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit $rc
